wy_mt_owen.blurb: Mount Owen is the second-highest summit in the Teton Range, rising to roughly 12,900 feet in the Cathedral Group inside Grand Teton National Park, with Valhalla Canyon along its western flank. This is mountain climbing rather than roadside cragging: most of the ten listed routes are alpine objectives, with a couple of ice lines and one trad route. The grade spread is wide, from fourth-class terrain and easy fifth class up to a handful of 5.10 lines, so the easiest way up is a scramble that suits competent mountaineers while the harder ridges and faces demand real alpine experience. Expect a long day with glacier and snow considerations.

wy_question_wall.blurb: Question Wall is a small sport crag in Ten Sleep Canyon, the big dolomite canyon east of the town of Ten Sleep. The face is slightly overhanging through its middle and eases back toward the right. All ten routes are bolted, and the grades start around 5.10 and stack up in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, so it is a place for people who already climb hard rather than a warm-up wall. Climbing here is on pockets, edges and flakes, and the wall picks up good shade through the afternoon, which helps on summer days. Allow about twenty minutes on foot from the road.

wy_queen_s_gambit.blurb: Queen's Gambit is a limestone slab in Swift Creek Canyon, on the North Fork trail near Jackson Hole. Ten bolted sport routes cover a broad range, from about 5.7 up to 5.12, with a good cluster around 5.9 and 5.10. The climbing is technical and thoughtful, in keeping with the chess-themed route names, and the wall steepens and loses features as you move from left to right. Bolting was laid out with newer leaders in mind, with friendly spacing on most lines and lowering hardware at the top. It sits a short stroll past the Hall of Hidden Kings and faces west, so plan on sun in the afternoon.

wy_road_10_rocks.blurb: Road 10 Rocks is a small cluster of eroded dolomite spires on the ridgeline above a Forest Service road in the Eastern Big Horns, close to the Highway 14 Pinnacles at about 9,500 feet. Ten routes are listed, a mix of trad and sport, ranging from an easy 5.5 up to one 5.12, with most between 5.8 and 5.11. The towers are friable, though a couple of patches have good rock, so test holds and take care with gear. It is a high, scenic and quiet spot where you are only minutes from the car; summer is the usual time, and afternoon thunderstorms are common.

wy_shadow_wall.blurb: Shadow Wall is a quiet limestone wall at the far end of the first band of trailside cliffs in Tongue River Canyon, just past the Music Wall. Ten routes are listed, six trad and four sport, covering roughly 5.6 through 5.11 with the biggest group at 5.10. Traffic here is light even though the canyon lines are good, so you often have it to yourself. The canyon as a whole suits all abilities and stays uncrowded, though south-facing walls there get very hot in summer. Reaching the wall is a bit longer and more roundabout than other sectors, along a cleared path at the cliff base that limits erosion.

wy_soda_fountain_wall.blurb: Soda Fountain Wall is a clean, nearly vertical sport wall in the East Bridge Bands, in Shoshone Canyon just west of Cody at around 6,000 feet. All ten routes are bolted and carry diner-themed names. They range from an easy-feeling 5.8 and a 5.9 through a pair of 5.10s, then a solid group of four 5.11s and two 5.12s, so the sweet spot is intermediate to hard climbers. The rock is south-facing dolomite, which makes it a warm choice and good for cooler days. Single-pitch climbing and a short walk make it a handy stop near town.
